notes.action_executions:
Contract cases of GET /api/actions/executions and the `executions` block of GET /api/battles/<id> (roadmap item 6, batch 2: r17a).

ONE new family of dashboard_contract_pages_v1.json, `action_executions`, generated by the real routes over a temporary ledger whose rows are written by the
real `ActionSession` / `Actions` (the same calls the collectors, the shopper and the harvest host make) on the world's fixed clock; nothing is the live ledger.

The history is the Dashboard's one generic read for every timed action: the page lists the executions of the emulator and account it is showing, newest first, and
renders any action from the row (action, instance, trigger, state, outcome, host, coverage, aggregate) without a branch per action.

  list           GET /api/actions/executions[?action=&action_instance=&battle_id=&before=&limit=&instance=]  ->  {schema_version, ledger_id, context, executions, truncated, next_before,
                 unusable}. Newest first in the order (start time, id), so rows of one start time are ordered and a cursor never loses one. `limit` 1..500 (default 50), `before` is a
                 `next_before` cursor or a bare start time (strictly older rows), anything else a coded 400 {ok:false, code:"invalid_request", error}. The account is part of the query: a
                 row of another account on the same device, and a row of another device, are never returned. `unusable` counts the damaged rows the page skipped.
  cold           a checkout with no ledger, and a ledger that never recorded an execution, answer an empty list with ledger_id null and create nothing.
  newer schema   a ledger a newer build wrote is not interpreted: executions [], reason "newer_schema", ledger_schema_version; status stays readable.
  battle detail  GET /api/battles/<id> carries `executions` {items (newest first), reason, truncated}: items null with reason "recorded_before_action_history" for a battle created before
                 the action store existed (which is not a battle where nothing ran), "newer_schema" on a newer ledger; rows of a battle a driver ADOPTED say coverage "since_adoption".

Two states have no producer and are made by writing the ledger the way a future build or a failing disk would: a row whose body is not JSON (the damaged-row count) and
`action_meta.schema_version` above this build's. Every other row is made by the writer. Not recorded: the refresher's settlement (no route triggers it; test_action_executions_route.py).
notes.action_executions_more:
Contract cases that complete the executions history (roadmap item 6, A2-7 backend requests B4, B6, B7 and B8; r17b).

ONE new family of dashboard_contract_pages_v1.json, `action_executions_more`, generated by the real routes over a temporary ledger, beside `action_executions` (whose
cases are unchanged except that every row now carries its action's `label`, request B9):

  run now          the battle detail lists the execution a Run now command started: its row carries that command's id (`command_id`), trigger manual, and the page can follow
                   the item `last.command_id` of runtime.actions to it (battle_actions_projection.run_now_completed_links_its_execution is the same battle's other half);
  cut off          a battle with more executions than a page holds: `executions.truncated` is true and `next_before` is the cursor the generic route continues from
                   (GET /api/actions/executions?battle_id=<id>&before=<next_before>); a complete block has no `next_before` key;
  settled          a driver that died with an execution open: the refresher (the dashboard's tick, never a GET) settles the row `interrupted`, with `finished_at` and `duration_ms`
                   null and the reason it was settled, and the battle detail says the same;
  harvest launch   the dashboard's launch attempts of the standalone collector are rows too (action `harvest_launch`, driver `dashboard`): a refusal before any operation exists
                   (the emulator is offline: `refused`, no operation) and a launch (`succeeded`, with the operation it started).
notes.ad_gems_failed_attempt_poll: r12d (gap of F6-11 6.4): GET /api/battles/active runtime.routines.ad_gems when the failed attempt was made by the collector own poll(frame) on the world clock (only the device boundary is faked: frames, the recognizer rectangle, the window list, capture and tap). battle_details_runtime finished its attempt by calling _finish_attempt directly, so its scheduling_wait_sec / response_delay_sec are null and response_wait_sec / response_overdue_sec absent; here all four are set (6.0 / 15.0 / 15.0 / 0), appearance_after_at is set because the HUD showed no offer on the first checks, and response_due_at / response_started_at are set while the response waits (the first case) and null once the attempt started (the offer is forgotten when an attempt begins). Recorded failures: not_confirmed / offer_still_visible after one tap (verification_before_tap_sec, verification_sec), and three skips with no tap: offer_moved (center_displacement_px, observed_rect, fresh_rect), in_front:<package> (visible_windows) and fresh_offer_missing (visibility absent). A refused tap or a capture error also fails an attempt but carries a Python traceback with this machine paths, so it is not recorded.
notes.battle_details_runtime: GET /api/battles/active with a Floating gems last_refusal recorded by the tapper's own refusal path and an Ad gems offer that was seen and whose attempt failed (visibility visible, first_seen_at, appearance_after_at, last_observed_at, response_due_at, last_failed_attempt, counters, durations).
notes.calibrate_writes: POST /api/calibrate/start | observe | apply | stop. EVERY refusal of these routes is {ok:false, code, error[, operation][, missing]}: the message is what the route always said, `code` is the stable word to branch on, `operation` (public form) is present when the refusal names the operation as it is now (the Stop contract). Codes: invalid_request (400: a body that is not a JSON object, not valid JSON, empty on start), invalid_routes | invalid_phases | invalid_watch (400), context_changed, idempotency_key_reused, operation_active (the ledger already holds an operation on the device), calibration_running, taps_disabled, navigation_images_missing (with `missing`, sorted), modules_not_done, device_owned | action_lock (unchanged), operation_required | operation_unknown | operation_changed | not_a_calibration | observations_tracked | starter_profile | profile_missing | profile_changed | restoration_pending | no_observations | artifact_unavailable | artifact_changed | artifact_invalid | apply_failed (apply; the last is 400 for a write that failed and 500 for anything unexpected, both return the operation to awaiting_apply). Launch commands carry expected_context and idempotency_key (an identical retry answers the stored operation, without `phases`, whatever has changed since). Start checks, in order: the action lock; the body (must be a JSON object, whatever the content type); routes (400); the receipt replay; owners (409 device_owned); a running calibration; taps (unless allow_navigation); phases; missing navigation images; phase e needs phase 1 modules; then the ledger (expected_context, another operation owns the device). Observe needs no taps; a body that does not claim to be JSON (or is empty) is an empty command, a body that claims to be JSON must be an object; `watch` is validated AFTER the receipt replay (an identical retry answers the stored operation) and before the owner checks, and must be a whole number of seconds from 0 to 600 (absent, null or 0: two frames only), anything else is refused, never clamped. Apply: a repeat of an applied revision is answered from the record (200); then owners, revision, original context and configuration revision, starter, profile file, sealed artifacts, no account observations or a pending module restoration (400, refused before the apply began: the operation is unchanged), write failures (400/500 apply_failed, the operation returns to awaiting_apply). A failed or interrupted capture is applied and keeps its failure. Stop is cooperative for calibrations (a marker file; status cancelling, stop.state stopping, nothing signalled), is not held back by the action lock, and a worker that cannot be verified is released while the lease is free. A worker proven gone is retired by the ledger before the revision is compared, so the Stop is refused operation_changed with the retired operation.
notes.collection_first_policy: Finding F6C-R1-04. A profile with no gathering policies takes its first one through the supported path that needs no backend change: GET /api/run-templates publishes the shipped defaults at templates[i].policies.gather[<reference>] (farm/tournament/dissonance `all_on`, shard `gems_only`), and POST /api/profile-patch {name, path:[policies, gather, <new name>], value, expected_revision} creates it (a missing mapping step is created, so an empty gather map or no gather key both work). A name already taken is REPLACED, not refused: the page must not offer a taken name. The empty policy is refused (gem_delay_sec is required); text, an unknown key and a stale revision are refused.
notes.context_fence: Review finding F6PE-P02. POST /api/accounts (select and create), /api/account-tier, /api/profile-activate, /api/profile-copy, /api/profile-promote, /api/profile-patch and /api/loadout-patch accept an optional `expected_context` {instance, account, profile, serial} (exactly these four keys, each text or null; the values GET /api/config names: active_instance, that instance's account and serial, active_profile). It is the FIRST check after the body is read (before the owner refusal, the validators and the revision checks) and is made under the config write lock, which stays held until the handler has written or refused. A mismatch is 409 {ok:false, code:'context_changed', error, current_context} (null when the configuration names no context at all: an unknown account, a missing config.yaml - the fence only reads, a refusal never seeds it from the example - or a stored shape that is not a configuration) and nothing is written; a field that is present but malformed (not an object, other keys, a value that is not text or null, an explicit null) is 400 {ok:false, code:'invalid_request', error}; an absent field is the legacy page's request, answered exactly as before (no fence). A request resent after a lost answer meets the context its own commit made and is refused context_changed: nothing is applied twice. POST /api/loadout-patch also carries its own expected_revision (compare-and-set on config.yaml): the context is judged first, so a stale context with any revision is context_changed and only a current context with a stale revision is revision_conflict. Another process editing config.yaml is excluded by no lock (as before).
notes.emulator_bluestacks_inventory: GET /api/wizard/emulators over a bluestacks.conf with two instances (one stopped, one running) and POST /api/wizard/bluestacks/prepare for each. Appended as its own family because emulator_inventory (MuMu world) has no BlueStacks row. `running` is an HD-Player.exe with `--instance <key>`; `adb_enabled` is the GLOBAL switch (every instance of one file carries the same value); `display_ok` is the instance own framebuffer at 2560x1080@360. Prepare is refused 409 while ANY HD-Player.exe runs, whichever instance is named (the stopped instance too); with nothing running it writes the ADB switch and the named instance framebuffer, and an instance already prepared answers 200 with nothing changed and no backup.
notes.format: Each case is {request:{method, path, body?}, status, body}. A JSON body is the route's exact answer (keys sorted by Flask); a body that is not JSON (the default 500 page an unhandled exception produces in production, exception propagation off) is {text}; a request whose body is not JSON records the text that was sent. Ids are aliased in order of appearance; the scenario root is <root>; time is the fixed clock 1800000000 (2027-01-15 08:00 UTC). A case named read_* is the GET a client makes to settle a write; the name says which write it follows.
notes.history_detail: GET /api/battles/{id}?instance=. {battle, events, context}; a record of another emulator or account is a 404 "Battle does not belong to the selected emulator and account". Records are made by the real BattleSession; setup reports by interactions.loadout's builders, the stats capture by runtime.runlog.clipboard_provenance, collection evidence by BattleSession's own counting (what it does not count is a case). Evidence of another generation cannot be produced by any driver: collection_evidence_of_another_generation_written_through_the_ledger puts it there with the ledger's own writer to show the page that the record holds it.
notes.history_list: GET /api/battles?instance=&limit=&offset=&status=. Newest record first (rowid descending); the filter is applied before the page; limit is 1..200 and offset >= 0 (400 "Invalid battle pagination"), a text that is not an integer is a 400 carrying Python's own message, status is one of prepared|active|ended|interrupted (an empty text means all). The list is scoped to the emulator and account the request names; there is no total count. Pages here use limit 2 over five records: the semantics (final page, past the end) are the same at limit 21.
notes.loadout_restore: POST /api/loadout-patch with cards_restore and modules_restore (see settings_modules): the whole loadout body, config expected_revision and the reviewed expected_context; the config read after each save.
notes.loadout_restore_eligibility: r12b2 (review R1): POST /api/loadout-patch refuses a restore edit it cannot check. The profile validator reads the loadouts a run of the ACTIVE profile names and no others, so a body that sets, changes or clears `cards_restore` or `modules_restore` of any other loadout - or any loadout when there is no active profile - is 409 {ok:false, code:"restore_loadout_unused", loadout, restore_keys, active_profile, error} and writes nothing, whether the value looks valid or not (ownership is the point, not the value). Order of the checks: context, revision, the loadout exists (404), this guard, then the validator's problems (400). A body whose restore keys are as stored is not a restore edit and is judged as it always was.
notes.plan_removal_effects: r12d (gap of F6-11 6.5): what POST /api/profile-patch {path:["plan"], op:"delete"} changes beyond the profile: GET /api/runs lists the config combo run (the day-plan run) only while the profile has a plan section - the run leaves `runs` and `readiness` when the section is removed and returns when it is added back; the blueprint runs are identical before, after and after the add-back. Deleting plan.week or plan.days (either half) leaves a plan with no blocks and is 400 {ok:false, error, problems} with the validator text (uncoded), also when the section is already gone (the route deletes from an empty plan); nothing is written. GET /api/schedule/status was probed and not recorded: it reports the running scheduler last observation and stayed available after the removal in the synthetic world.
notes.plan_section_delete: POST /api/profile-patch {path:[plan], op:delete}: 200 and the profile without `plan`; deleting an absent plan section is also 200 (a new backup); a stale revision is 409.
notes.preview_backends: F6-13: GET /api/stream/backends reports local prerequisites only (MuMu native: a target or a reason; scrcpy: installed, decoder, reason, version, server_path; adb: the p10b report). Availability is not a connection: the transport-offline sample equals the available one, and the route talks to adb never. The scrcpy package states are produced from a synthetic server file and the real verification (a missing file reads "scrcpy server missing or unreadable: <path>", not the brief's proposed text). A saved preview setting that is invalid is 400 {ok:false, error}.
notes.preview_frame_png: F6-13: GET /api/frame.png with the headers it sends (the answers also exist in recognition_images, which records none): Content-Type only, no Cache-Control, and no age or source header; a failed capture is a text 502 (Flask's default text/html), an invalid display a 400 JSON.
notes.preview_status: F6-13: GET /api/stream/status?stream_id=. 200 WITHOUT an `ok` key (the session record: counters, timing, requested and actual backend, backend_failures [{backend, reason, stage}], frame_age_ms, active, last_error, last_frame_age_s, actual_fps); a session that never existed or was evicted is 404 {ok:false, error}. Sessions are made by the real stream route and read while its response is open, closed, stale or failing; the sources are synthetic (12x24 frames, 10 ms capture, 2 ms JPEG encode on the fixed clock, a scrcpy age of 50 ms when a frame completes) and fail or fall back through the real PreviewCapture. A status read between two parts is a snapshot: the part in flight is identified by its own headers, not by this record.
notes.preview_stream: F6-13: GET /api/stream.mjpg. 200 multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=frame, Cache-Control no-cache. Each part carries Content-Type, Content-Length and FOUR provenance headers made with the part's own pixels (added with this contract): X-Preview-Frame-Kind frame|error, X-Preview-Sequence (successful frames when the part was made; an error marker repeats the last number), X-Preview-Backend mumu|scrcpy|adb|unknown, X-Preview-Source-Age-Ms a number|unknown. A recorded stream is its response headers and its first parts, decoded (width, height, encoded_bytes and the sha256 of the decoded pixels; termination "recorder_closed" says the recorder ended it). The error marker is drawn text, so only its kind and size are recorded. HEAD validates and reserves nothing (empty body). Refusals are JSON {ok:false, error}: 400 invalid parameter or saved setting, 409 another emulator or an active duplicate id, 429 32 active sessions. There is no owner refusal: a stream starts while automation owns the screen and sends no input.
notes.profile_patch_fenced: r12d (F6-14b, root decision D4): every write of the Schedule, Collection, Abilities and Runs pages to the ACTIVE profile sends expected_context (the runtime context, as GET /api/config publishes it) and expected_revision (the source revision of `mine` it read). The route already honoured both; what was missing were recordings of those bodies for the active profile. Each success is followed by `read_after_<case>` (GET /api/profile-src/mine): the revision and the profile equal the write's answer, no problem. The refusal after the account switch is 409 {code:"context_changed", current_context: beta's} with nothing written (the read after it equals the read before). The inactive profile `second`, `theirs` and config.yaml are untouched by every case (asserted by the generator). The brief's table names 14 cases; 13 are successes and one the refusal; the 14 reads are extra.

notes.recognition_context_fence: POST /api/calibrate/apply takes the optional `expected_context` {instance, account, profile, serial} (the same fence as the Profiles writes): a mismatch is 409 context_changed + current_context and writes nothing, judged FIRST under the config write lock - before the owner refusal, the replay of an applied operation and the operation checks; a malformed field (null included) is 400 invalid_request; an absent field is the legacy request. An apply by operation_id is judged by the fence and then by the operation's own context check (409 context_changed without current_context). calibrate start / observe and screen-analysis start are refused by the operation's frozen five-field expected_context (no current_context); Stop is a revocation and is never refused for a context.
notes.recognition_images: A route that answers pixels is recorded as {binary:{content_type, width, height, pixels_sha256}}: the PNG's bytes depend on the encoder, the decoded pixels do not. The device shows a synthetic 1080x2560 frame drawn in the generator (gradient, a button-like block of integer-exact bars, one flat grey block); nothing was captured. The artwork text badge is drawn with anti-aliased text, so only its size and Cache-Control are recorded. GET /api/frame.png remembers the frame under ?ts= (the last 8 tokens) together with the page it was fetched for (instance, account, profile, serial); POST /api/template/<rel> crops that exact frame and refuses 409 frame_expired (the token is gone) or 409 frame_context_changed (the page changed since: the token stays valid for the page it was fetched for). The cropper's other refusals keep {ok:false, error}. The provenance of a crop (report entry with the image hash, learned rectangle) is read from the file the route wrote, under the dashboard's account; it no longer consults the settings singleton. Screen recognition (OCR) is a controlled stand-in.
notes.recognition_later: Later tools. POST /api/clicker/step answers {ok:true, result} with the worker's own verdict inside: result.ok can be false (refused, screen changed, click sent but destination not confirmed) under an outer ok:true; a worker that prints nothing is a nested refusal; one that prints no JSON or times out is the unknown outcome {ok:false, error:"Check did not finish..."} (HTTP 200). The body must be a JSON object (400 invalid_request; so is an action that is not text); `execute` must be the JSON true or false when present (400 invalid_execute otherwise, before any permission check) and only true clicks (409 taps_disabled when taps are off). GET /api/clicker/frame with no preview is 404 no_preview. GET /api/manifest/contribution downloads text only (verified geometry, counts of excluded entries, discovery candidates); the screen object the analyzer writes ({name, candidates}) is read by its name (a name the manifest does not know is "unclassified"), a plain name is read as well, and a report or analysis that is not the shape its producer writes is skipped.
notes.recognition_reads: GET /api/wizard/templates | required | scan-plan[?preset=], /api/catalogue/modules, /api/calibrate/status[?operation_id=]. The account-less root holds the digit font (10 files every world is seeded with); an account's own listing and plan count its images only. The module catalogue normally reads the machine's backend/catalogue_local.yaml: the cases point it at a file of the world (the learned modules of a real install are not part of the contract). The scan plan always lists all 209 targets with their status (Missing | Captured; recognition not yet verified | Verified on this emulator | Needs attention: <reason>); `required` marks only the blocking images of the named run; a calibrate_report.json that is not valid JSON, not an object, or whose entries are not objects with a `rel` verifies nothing (200). Status of an operation shows only artifacts sealed to it: a state of another operation empties state, report and manifests and names the artifact in artifact_errors; a shared file that is JSON but not an object reads as {}. Refusals of the status route carry codes operation_unknown | operation_kind_mismatch. Setup evidence (setup battle, final screen, report entries per target) is echoed as the calibrator wrote it; the route summarises no target gap and no scan metric (see NOT_PRODUCIBLE).
notes.run_controls_live: POST /api/operations/{id}/live-controls records one revisioned controls command for the tracked battle: compare-and-set on control_revision, one unapplied change at a time, idempotent by idempotency_key (an identical request is answered from its record after the driver or battle ended; the same key with other changes is a 409). 400/404/409 mean nothing was recorded; a recorded command whose read-back failed answers 500 command_outcome_unknown. The accepted cases also record the battle read that lists the command and the key. The command wire states (requested, pending, applied, rejected, expired) are in dashboard_contract_v1.json battles_active.
notes.run_controls_live_reset_all: POST /api/operations/{id}/live-controls with null for several paths in one request resets them together (a null for a path with no override is accepted). After a reset `overrides` keeps the (empty) routine mappings: no override means no LEAF, not an empty object.
notes.run_controls_live_reset_all_mixed: r12c (F6-11 RL2): ONE live-controls request that sends null for `shopping_plan` AND for the routine overrides applied together, from the applied mixed state of shopping_queue.shopping_plan_routine_overrides_applied (routine overrides shopping off / every 60 s at revision 1, the plan PW at revision 2). A null removes the override: the plan returns to the battle's starting plan and the routines to their starting values, the three paths in one command; `overrides` keeps the (empty) routines mapping and no `shopping_plan` key. The same request with only the plan keeps the routine overrides, with only the routines keeps the plan override; a stale control revision is a 409 that keeps both; the identical resend is answered from the record.
notes.run_controls_save: POST /api/run-controls saves the SAVED run (the profile file), compare-and-set on the file revision. Order of the route's checks: no usable active profile (400), starter/draft/other account (409), context (409), revision (409), then the values (400). The reply is the read's shape with the new profile_revision. There is no idempotency key: a request whose answer was lost is settled by a read, never by sending it again (the identical resend of a committed save is refused as stale). A save that raised after the file was written answers a text 500 and the read shows it; one that raised before the write answers the same 500 and the read shows the old revision. Non-finite numbers (the JSON words for not-a-number and infinity) cannot be written in this strict-JSON fixture; the route refuses them with 400 (asserted by the generator, not recorded).
notes.run_entry_patch: POST /api/profile-patch on [blueprints, <run>, <field>] for a coin, a tournament, a shard and a dissonance coin run. The 500 answers here are the route's own JSON {ok:false, error} (validator unavailable / write failed), not the default error page. A stale revision is judged before the values.
notes.run_entry_patch_parity: r12c (F6-11 RL9, RL12, RL13; legacy rows R-25, R-26, R-30): POST /api/profile-patch on [blueprints, <run>, <field>], the way the legacy page wrote them. label: a delete (op:"delete") makes the run identifier show again and is accepted even when there is no label; an empty, blank or non-text label is refused; a label or an identifier that title-cased is another run's name is refused, and so is deleting a label when the identifier would then repeat another run's label. kind: a dissonance run IS a coin run with `dissonant_tab` - set, retargeted, deleted (op:"delete") to go back; a bare value null is STORED as null (the key stays; the page deletes instead); an unknown tab is refused. `kind` itself is refused: by the validator while the run keeps a field of the old kind (coin-only fields, the as_is equipment) and, since r12d, by the route's own guard (400 kind_change_refused) for a coin run that keeps none - it used to be saved (family run_kind_guard has the full set). limits: `rides` of an Ultimate Weapon grant quest and `cycles` of a cycle quest are integers >= 1; rides may be deleted, cycles may not (required); the other kind's field and `count` are refused (count names rides / cycles).
notes.run_kind_guard: r12d (F6-11 RL12, the r12c review): a run's kind picks its runner and decides which fields it may carry, so POST /api/profile-patch refuses a patch that changes the kind of a run that exists before and after it. A change by the `kind` field, by replacing the whole run, or by replacing the whole `blueprints` mapping is 400 {ok:false, code:"kind_change_refused", error, changes:[{blueprint, from_kind, to_kind}]} (sorted by run name; a deleted kind would be to_kind null), nothing written. It is judged after the revision and context checks (409 revision_conflict / context_changed come first) and after the validator: a change the validator already refuses (an unknown or deleted kind, a field the new kind may not carry, the as_is equipment on a non-coin run, a shard-only count) keeps the validator's own answer, uncoded, with `problems`. Not kind changes, and accepted: setting the kind a run already has, replacing a whole run by one of the same kind, adding a run (any kind), removing one - and removing a run and adding it again as another kind, which are two requests (a plan block that names the run blocks the first). Before r12d the same patch of a coin run that kept no coin-only field to a tournament run was saved (run_entry_patch_parity recorded it).
notes.run_templates_add: POST /api/run-templates/add has no expected_revision and no idempotency key: an identical resend after a committed add is 400 "That run already exists"; a lost answer is settled only by reading the profile. Every refusal and failure is 400 except a starter/draft profile (409); a write that fails after the file changed is also 400.
notes.run_templates_add_coded: r12c (F6-11 part 2 / RL4): POST /api/run-templates/add with a guard (`expected_revision` and/or `expected_context`) carries a stable `code` on every refusal the route can PROVE happened before anything was written, so a page may show it as Refused: id_taken (400: the run identifier, or a policy that identifier would create, exists), recipe_refused (400: not an identifier, unknown template, an unsupported or malformed choice), validation_failed (400: the profile validator refused the result; `problems` stays), profile_unavailable (400: no such profile, unreadable, not UTF-8, not a mapping, a name that is not a profile name; 409: the starter and a scan draft) and write_failed_nothing_saved (400: the write raised AND the profile file is byte-identical to what it was before the attempt). revision_conflict (409), context_changed (409) and invalid_request (400) are the guards' own, unchanged, and are judged first. A failure after which the file differs, or cannot be read back, has NO code (written_then_the_answer_failed_has_no_code): its outcome is unknown and a read of the profile settles it. A request WITHOUT a guard is answered exactly as before, without a code (the unguarded_* cases). The same requests are in run_templates_add (unguarded, unchanged) and run_templates_add_fenced, where six answers gained the code.
notes.run_templates_add_fenced: POST /api/run-templates/add gained two OPTIONAL guards (root-approved behaviour change; absent = the legacy request, answered as before, see run_templates_add): `expected_revision` (the profile revision as GET /api/profile-src publishes it) is judged under the profile lock BEFORE the recipe: stale, null, empty or not text is 409 revision_conflict with the current revision, nothing written; a request that carries it also gets the new `revision` back in the 200 answer. `expected_context` {instance, account, profile, serial} is the fence of the other context-dependent writes (409 context_changed + current_context, judged first; malformed or null 400 invalid_request). The resend of a committed add carrying the old revision is 409; without it the run identifier refuses it (400).
notes.runtime_environment: Item 10 p10b. GET /api/runtime carries `environment` (local prerequisites: operating system, interpreter, release kind, platform-tools with the version of a MATCHING install receipt only, emulator locators, scrcpy server and decoder, app build, OCR script and the stored OCR probe result); GET /api/stream/backends reports adb and scrcpy; POST /api/environment/probe with exactly {"probe": "windows_ocr"} runs the one OCR probe, under the global action lock. Every host input is pinned in the test world and every file the report reads is created under <root>/install, so the family is the same on every machine: the operating system, Python, adb (platform-tools) and scrcpy versions in it are the pins of the code or the values the world was given, never read from the machine that generated it. `available` is a local prerequisite, not a working emulator connection or capture; a locator that finds nothing is `unknown`; an OCR script is present without OCR being known to work until the probe says so. The family runtime_state records the same field (over an empty root) and keeps its place.
notes.runtime_release: Item 10 p10a. GET /api/runtime carries `release` beside `server` (`server` is this process against the source on disk now). `release` (runtime/build_info.release_identity) is what the tree the server runs from says it is: kind `checkout` (no release_identity.json; every other field null) or the `source` / `portable-windows-x64` identity its build wrote (version, source fingerprint, app-build and lock hashes, python for the portable build, build time, git revision, working-tree state), always with the same keys, plus `matches_source` (the recorded fingerprint against the source on disk now) and `matches_app_build` (every file under frontend/webui/app against BUILD_INVENTORY.txt, and that inventory against the recorded hash), each true, false (edited, added or missing) or null (not applicable, or the files cannot be read), and `error` (why the kind is `unknown`). `environment.release` stays the kind alone. The families runtime_state and runtime_environment record the same field over trees that recorded nothing (every field null) or whose record says nothing but a kind; this family is the installs, each a small synthetic tree of the world (a source file, a built app with its BUILD_INVENTORY.txt and the identity naming both), edited, extended or damaged state by state. It is a new family, appended last, because the hashes an install carries are aliased in order of appearance and would renumber every family after them.
notes.screen_analysis: POST /api/screen-analysis/start does not consult the process table (the ledger refuses a second operation: 409 operation_active); a body must be a JSON object or empty / not claim to be JSON. Every refusal of start, status and frame carries a code (idempotency_key_reused | context_changed | operation_active | operation_unknown | operation_kind_mismatch | analysis_not_finished | artifact_unavailable | artifact_changed | artifact_invalid); status and frame follow the requested operation, else the latest of the context, else the shared files. A running operation reports status running whatever the file says; a file of another operation is not shown (message "belongs to another operation" stays in the reply next to status running); failed or interrupted operations are status error with the operation's message or "Analysis did not complete"; a finished operation whose result was never written is status unavailable. frame.png ignores the `revision` query the page may send; with no operation and no file it is 404 no_screenshot.
notes.settings_modules: F6-15 / r12b: the cases the brief names settings.<case> and loadout_patch.<case> are in the NEW families settings_modules and loadout_restore, under the brief's own case names: appended families keep every published family's ids and hash. GET/POST /api/settings gained seven typed modules, so EVERY snapshot in the `settings` family now lists them (that is why the family `settings` changed): instance-defaults (label, default preset, autostart of the selected emulator), active-instance (the selected emulator), run-defaults (the machine fallback preset), tournament-cards (the standing deck drop/add lists; a `string-list` field: ordered, non-blank strings, `maxItems` 50, nothing coerced or deduplicated) and loop-defaults, missions-defaults, fleet-defaults (the ROOT blocks, apart from the selected emulator's override, which the modules loop, missions and fleet keep editing). Preset choices are the runnable presets (a placeholder is not offered) and the instance default also offers the empty value "Use machine fallback". A bound account's tournament lists are saved under that account. Saving active-instance is a selection-only write: the stored configuration differs from before in `active_instance` and nothing else, so no account record changes, whatever it stores (a sparse record is not filled in; settings_switch_records); an emulator whose account is unknown is refused before anything is written. A stale revision or context is 409 whatever the values; one invalid field writes none. The restore values cards_restore and modules_restore are keys of a loadout body validated like `cards` and `modules` (the card preset must be on the account, the module owned), and are editable only on a loadout a run of the ACTIVE profile names (loadout_restore_eligibility).
notes.settings_modules_more: r12e (the open recording requests of F6-15, compliance C-03): what settings_modules and loadout_restore did not record. Every request is POST /api/settings {context, revision, module, values} (the reads are GET /api/settings, or GET /api/config where the name says so) over the worlds of settings_modules (alpha on main, beta on other; presets normal_run, coin_farm and the placeholder `later`). The published families are unchanged: a read the page needs "just before" a published save (read_before_saved_instance_defaults, read_before_saved_modules_restore, read_before_the_clearing_refusal, and the state the published saved_tournament_cards leaves) is recorded here in a world that reaches the same bytes, and test_the_reads_of_settings_modules_more_are_the_states_the_published_saves_start_from compares its revision with the published request. saved_instance_defaults_with_fallback_and_autostart_off is {preset:"", autostart:false} sent from the state the published save leaves: the catalogue has no boolean `fallback`; "fallback" is the explicit option "Use machine fallback" (the empty preset), stored as the empty string, and autostart is stored as an explicit false. Machine defaults over an override: run-defaults, loop-defaults, missions-defaults and fleet-defaults write the ROOT value only; the selected emulator's own values (its default preset, instances.main.loop|missions|fleet) and the other emulator are byte-identical afterwards, and the emulator module (`loop`, `missions`, `fleet`) still shows its override - a key the override does not carry (loop.dry_run, fleet.post_window) follows the new default. Preset choices: an enum offers exactly the catalogue options - run-defaults the runnable presets (a `defined: false` placeholder is not one), instance-defaults those plus the empty value "Use machine fallback" - and any other value is 400 {ok:false, error:"<label>: expected enum"} (run-defaults: "Fallback preset: expected enum", instance-defaults: "Default preset: expected enum"; uncoded), whatever its type, with nothing written, also the valid fields of the same request. Only the fields a request names are validated: a stored preset that is no longer offered (a hand-edited name) stays, and is shown with an options list that lacks it, until a request names it, so a form that sends every field back is refused while a save without the preset field is 200. With no runnable preset (all placeholders, or no `presets` in the configuration) run-defaults offers an empty list and refuses every value, the one it shows included; instance-defaults offers only the empty value and saves it. Tournament lists: tournament-cards stores the lists as sent, [] included (saved_tournament_cards_empty_lists sets every string list of the module to []); with an account bound to the selected emulator they are the account's (the root block, the legacy default, and the other account are untouched), with none they are the root block; a save that changes nothing is 200 with the same revision. The two GET /api/config reads are the configuration the loadout restore requests start from; the request that follows each is replayed unrecorded by the generator to prove the read admits it.
notes.settings_modules_more_2: r12f (the follow-up of F6-15): three recordings the settings and equipment pages still needed. (1) saved_modules_restore_only is POST /api/loadout-patch {name:"plain", expected_revision, expected_context {account:null, instance:"main", profile:"mine", serial:"fake:1"}, body {cards:"main_farm", cards_restore:"no_card", modules_restore:[["black_hole_digestor","assist"]]}} from the state settings_modules_more.read_before_saved_modules_restore records (the cards restore is saved; the guard test compares the revision of that read with the request). (3) A tournament list holding [false, 7, "keep"] from hand-edited YAML is shown by GET /api/settings as stored (raw); saving it back is 400 "Cards to drop: entry 1 must be a non-blank string" (uncoded, nothing written); a save that names only the other list is 200 and the malformed list stays as stored (only the fields a request names are validated); a save that names the list with valid entries repairs it. The same lists saved again are 200 with the same revision.
notes.settings_switch_records: r12b2 (review R2): saving the active-instance module writes only `active_instance`. Over accounts that store only what they were given (no loadouts, no tweaks, an unsorted profile list, no profile list) every record is exactly as it was, in the file and in the configuration read afterwards; the answer is the snapshot of the new context.
notes.shopping_queue: F6-12: every case of the brief under the brief's own names. The saved queue is POST /api/run-controls changes.shopping_plan, the live queue POST /api/operations/{id}/live-controls, manual shopping POST /api/operations/{id}/actions, the shared library POST /api/profile-patch on policies.shopping_lists.<id>. notes.shopping_queue_bounds: r12c (F6-12 SQ5): what the SERVER answers to a shopping queue whose per-entry numbers are out of bounds, through the saved run save (POST /api/run-controls) and the live save (POST /api/operations/{id}/live-controls); both validate the plan with the same rules and refuse with 400 {ok:false, error}, recording nothing (a read after them shows the saved run unchanged and no command). tap_limit: an integer >= 0 (negative, fraction, text and booleans are refused); weight: an integer from 1 to 100 ("expected integer >= 1" for 0, a fraction or text; "from 1 to 100" above 100); from_wave an integer >= 1, until_wave an integer >= 2 and greater than from_wave (a reversed or empty range is "<id>: empty wave range"). The smallest and largest accepted values are saved and applied in boundary_values_accepted.
